rules.rule: This is a Next.js Server Action file; every exported "use server" function is a PUBLIC endpoint. Flag any exported action whose first work is not an authorisation check via requirePermission()/can() from lib/auth/can.ts. Flag inline role checks such as `session.user.role === ...` (all authorisation must go through can(), ADR 0004). Actions must return ActionResult via ok()/err() for expected failures and only throw for real bugs. Input must be validated with the shared Zod schema from lib/schemas before use. A lookup of an event the user is not related to must return the same not-found result as a missing one, so ids cannot be probed (SCRUM-68). Status changes must be conditional on the observed current status so concurrent actions cannot both win (ADR 0006); counted pools such as equipment or registration capacity need SELECT ... FOR UPDATE inside a transaction (ADR 0007). Also check correctness, missing boundary conditions, N+1 queries, and SQL/XSS injection risks.

This is the single authorisation module (ADR 0004). Check BOTH the role gate (ROLE_ACTIONS) and the relationship gate for every Action: a coordinator sees only assigned events or unassigned non-draft ones, an organiser only their own, an attendee only their own registrations. Flag any path that fails open (a missing or undefined field treated as permission granted). Flag any role granted an action it should not have. Check that tests cover every disallowed role.

Flag any edit to a migration.sql inside an existing prisma/migrations/<timestamp>_*/ folder: applied migrations must never be edited; fix forward with a new migration. New String[] columns need @default([]). Check that schema.prisma and the migration SQL agree, that foreign keys used in filters have an @@index, and that domain rules enforced in the database (EXCLUDE USING gist with [) half-open ranges, CHECK constraints) are not weakened. No hard deletes: lifecycle changes are status changes. Flag anything in seed.ts that could not safely run against the shared database.

ConnectSphere is a Next.js 16 App Router + Prisma + Auth.js app. Check correctness, missing boundary conditions, error handling, race conditions, security (XSS, injection, leaking another user's data), N+1 queries, and whether critical logic has tests. Project conventions to enforce: no hard-coded colours (no hex, rgb() or Tailwind palette classes like bg-slate-100 or text-emerald-700; use theme tokens such as bg-muted, text-success); never format dates inline with toLocaleString, use formatDate/formatDateTime from lib/datetime; datetimes are stored as UTC, so a datetime-local value must be converted to a UTC ISO instant in the browser before it is sent to the server; no inline role checks in components or pages (authorisation goes through lib/auth/can.ts); no new dependencies without an ADR; comments explain why, not what. Tests must trace to a SCRUM key and a test that only exercises a mock of the database proves nothing.
